<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" /></noinclude><section begin=par155 />verb {{GHGheb|text=אֶל־הַמָּקוֹם אֲשֶׁר}}; after {{GHGheb|text=בְּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=2|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=1|verse=4}} ({{GHGheb|text=בַּֽהֵכִין}}={{GHGheb|text=בְּהַֽה׳}}=''to the place where''); after {{GHGheb|text=לְ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=65|verse=1}} {{GHGheb|text=לְלוֹא שָׁאָ֫לוּ}} by them ''that asked not'' for me... {{GHGheb|text=לְלֹא בִקְשֻׁ֫נִי}} them ''that sought me not''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=13|verse=3}} that which ''they have not seen'', but the text is hardly correct; after {{GHGheb|text=עַל}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=119|verse=136}}, cf. {{GHGpar|158|b}}; after {{GHGheb|text=עִם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=16|verse=9}}.—A noun-clause follows {{GHGheb|text=לְ}} in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Neh|chapter=8|verse=10}}. An analogous instance in Aramaic is {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ezr|chapter=5|verse=14}} ''to'' one ''whose name was Sheshbazzar'' [so in the papyri, see the Lexicon, p. 1116<sup>a</sup>].<section end=par155 />

<section begin=par156 />{{GHGpar-heading|156|Circumstantial Clauses}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|156|a}}
'''1.''' The statement of the particular circumstances under which a subject appears as performing some action, or under which an action (or an occurrence) is accomplished, is made especially (apart from relative clauses, see § 155) by means of noun-clauses connected by {{GHGterm|Wāw}} with a following subject (see further on this kind of ''circumstantial clause'' in {{GHGpar|141|e}}), and by verbal-clauses (see {{GHGpar|142|d}}). Very frequently, however, such statements of the particular circumstances are subordinated to the main clause by being simply attached, without {{GHGterm|Wāw}}, either as noun-clauses, sometimes extremely short (see c), or as verbal-clauses (see d–g).

{{GHGmargin-letter|156|b}}
Rem. Among relative clauses of this kind the commonest are the various noun-clauses, which are most closely subordinated to a preceding substantive without {{GHGheb|text=אֲשֶׁר}}, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=16|verse=12}}; also statements of weight, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=22}}; of name, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=1|verse=1}} (also introduced by {{GHGheb|text=וּשְׁמוֹ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=24|verse=29}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=1|verse=1}}, &c., or {{GHGheb|text=וּשְׁמָהּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=16|verse=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=22|verse=24|hidebook=1}}, &c.); of a condition of body, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=1|verse=7}}, and others.—Noun-clauses which begin with {{GHGterm|wāw}} and the ''predicate'' have a somewhat more independent character than those introduced by {{GHGterm|wāw}} and the ''subject''<ref>In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=32|verse=31}} this form of sequence appears to be selected for another purpose, ''and indeed our enemies are judges'' thereof, with {{GHGterm|wāw emphatic}}; to take it as a circumstantial clause is too artificial.</ref> ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=19|verse=1}}, &c.). The former, however, are also to be regarded as circumstantial clauses, in so far as they describe a ''state'' which is simultaneous with the principal action; thus {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=3|verse=7}} ''I will not be an healer'', {{GHGheb|text=וּבְבֵיתִי אֵין לֶ֫חֶם|translate=while in my house is neither bread nor clothing}}; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=6|verse=6}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Am|chapter=7|verse=7}}); {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=13|verse=18}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=16|verse=1|hidebook=1}}. Cf. also the instances in {{GHGpar|152|l}} of {{GHGheb|text=וְאֵין}} followed by a participle, as {{GHGheb|text=וְאֵין מַצִּיל}}, &c.

{{GHGmargin-letter|156|c}}
'''2.''' Characteristic examples of circumstantial ''noun''-clauses are {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=12|verse=8}} ''and pitched his tent'' {{GHGheb|text=בֵּֽית־אֵל מִיָם וְהָעַי מִקֶּ֫דֶם}} with ''Bethel on the west and Ai on the east''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=22|verse=24}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=18|verse=14}} ''through the heart of Absalom'', {{GHGheb|text=עוֹדֶנּ֫וּ חַי}} while ''he'' was ''yet alive''; {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=30|verse=6}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=9|verse=2}} (cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=3|verse=8}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Na|chapter=3|verse=8}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=14|verse=5}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 Ch|chapter=23|verse=10}}; with the predicate preceding, e.g. {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=26|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=32|verse=8}}.—In {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=41|verse=29}} a noun-clause serves to announce a state in the future.—We may also include here certain set phrases, as {{GHGheb|text=פָּנִים אֶל־פָּנִים|translate=face to face}} (prop. while ''face'' was turned ''towards face''), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=32|verse=31}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=33|verse=11}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dt|chapter=34|verse=10}},<section end=par156 /><noinclude>
